manuscript.title: Every complex K3 surface is Oka
literal_fragments: None of these assertions requires an
upper bound for the $L_j$ or a bound on the number of blocks.

quantifiers.inputs: For every 0<h<1/8, r>0, A>=0 and every bi-infinite sequence L_j>=1, and every chain of the stated periodic symplectic charts with exact degree-one transitions.
quantifiers.uniformity: The error threshold and b depend only on h,r,A and fixed initial margins, not on j, any L_j, or the number of blocks.
quantifiers.conclusion: For every error e<e_star the full stated normal form and periodic symplectic immersion exist on C times Delta_b.
quantifiers.passive_extension: The same constants work jointly holomorphically over an arbitrary passive complex parameter manifold when all active-coordinate hypotheses and sup bounds hold uniformly there.

constants.limiting_margin_lower_bound: 7/16 times the original h or r

adversarial_probes.family: E=(w,p+epsilon*z), z=exp(k*w), k=2*pi*i*n, n a nonzero integer; J=(w+a0+s*p**2,p)
adversarial_probes.check: F=J composed with E is exactly symplectic and has the displayed exact Liouville primitive for all symbolic parameters; the correct shear-conjugated cancellation has zero first-order residual.
adversarial_probes.scope: A universal local exact family, not a purported counterexample or a finite-exhaustion proof.

adversarial_probes.check: Its Liouville period is c, so the apparent accumulating transverse drift violates the theorem's exactness hypothesis.
adversarial_probes.scope: Excluded nonexact boundary case, not an admissible counterexample.

jacobian.mathematical_scope: Exact first derivative of the transverse-dependent shear (w+s*p**2,p); not the infinite-dimensional sewing theorem.
